rationale: Pivot from xgb_day_quality_consensus (20-iter sweep #691-710 saturated at avg_ann ~0%, only iter #688's xgb_recency_consensus hit 5/7 +27%). torch_seq_gru default produced 1/7 +22% — comparable on windows passed but +22pp in avg_ann, and crucially is the first non-tabular trainer (consumes_sequences=True). W3 +122% / W6 +96% / W7 +75% prove the temporal inductive bias finds signal the XGB-aggregate family cannot. Failures are all WR<40% (model is too aggressive) — train mode should sweep pos_class_weight ∈ [1.0, 3.5] and dropout ∈ [0.25, 0.45] to trade selectivity for win quality. Even modest WR lift on W3/W6/W7 (3.5pp each) would push 4/7 windows over the per-window gate.
